rationale: The question is what happens to people who choose supported tapering, measured as they go, with deliberate follow-up of those who leave. A prospective observational design fits: the pathway is already offered to everyone eligible, the outcomes can be collected at existing calls, and prospective collection gives consistent pain interference and withdrawal data that the clinic notes lack. The retrieved evidence supports pharmacist contact as the exposure (c1), emergency visits and overdose as balancing outcomes (c2) and distance and language as predictors of leaving (c3). Reporting follows STROBE.
alternatives: Randomised comparison of pathway support against unsupported tapering (refused: withholding support from people who want it is not acceptable and everyone eligible is already offered the pathway)
Retrospective review of the first year's clinic notes (refused as the main design: pain interference and withdrawal were not recorded consistently; useful as a feasibility check)
Before-after comparison with patients who tapered before July 2025
whyNotMoreComplex: A comparative design would need an unsupported group the clinic does not have and would not accept; a descriptive follow-up with pre-specified outcomes answers what the hospital needs for its 2027 decision.

decision.statement: Follow every adult who enters the pharmacist-led tapering pathway from November 2026 for 12 months in a prospective observational study, with percent change in daily dose at 6 months as the primary outcome and pain interference, withdrawal, disengagement, emergency visits and overdose as secondary and balancing outcomes.
decision.question: Should the clinic run a prospective observational study of the pharmacist-led tapering pathway?

criteria.text: Pharmacist contact during tapering has been followed by more dose reduction and fewer patients leaving care, and the predictors of leaving are known well enough to plan data collection.
Emergency visits for withdrawal or overdose rise among pathway patients during the first months of the taper.

gates.requirement: Research ethics board approval of the protocol
Pharmacist time to collect outcomes at the fortnightly calls
gates.evidence: Allocation letter VGH-PC-2025-07: 0.4 FTE funded until 2028-03-31, supplied by the investigator

alternatives: Retrospective review of the first year's clinic notes
Before-after comparison with patients who tapered before July 2025
decision.note: Rests on ledger claims c1 to c3 from retrieved records; the ethics gate is unmet until the board approves.

summary: Prospective observational study recommended; the decision rests on three ledger claims and waits for ethics approval.
